results.claim: Patsy centering of x1 and standardising of x0 are stateful: new data must be transformed with the in-sample mean and std via build_design_matrices.
results.quote: These are called stateful transformations, because you must use statistics like the mean or standard deviation of the original dataset when transforming a new dataset.

limits: Authors say it is not comprehensive; each library merits its own book.

Dated: statsmodels sm.tsa.AR was removed (replaced by AutoReg/AutoRegResults, ARIMA) in later statsmodels; np.linalg.lstsq(X, y) now warns without rcond=None; LogisticRegression repr shows multi_class='ovr', solver='liblinear', n_jobs=1 of 2017 sklearn; Patsy is in maintenance, formulaic is a successor; DataFrame.values superseded by .to_numpy(); chapter admits sklearn has no deep pandas integration (since changed: set_output('pandas'), ColumnTransformer). Judged from knowledge outside the text, not from the chapter.
Titanic imputation uses the median Age, with no claim the model is good: 'I make no claims that this is a good model'.
No test accuracy is computed (y_true unavailable).
practices: Use .values only for homogeneous data; heterogeneous frames become object arrays (p.385).
Select model columns with data.loc[:, cols].values (p.385).
Prefer Patsy over hand-built get_dummies for non-numeric columns, less error-prone (p.386).
Use + 0 to suppress intercept; with an intercept Patsy drops one category level to avoid collinearity (pp.388, 391).
Wrap arithmetic in I() inside formulas since + means term inclusion (p.390).
Reapply stateful transforms to held-out data with build_design_matrices and saved design_info (p.389).
Reattach column names to coefficients via X.design_info.column_names (p.388).
Fill missing values before statsmodels/sklearn and use training-set statistics for both train and test (p.399).
Use cross-validation (cross_val_score, LogisticRegressionCV) to tune and avoid overfitting (p.400-401).
Consult current docs, since books go out of date (p.401).
